definition: The order in which people notice elements on a screen, created on purpose with size, weight, color, position and space so the most important content is seen first.
The Gestalt principle that elements placed close together are seen as related. In UI design it means space inside a group must be smaller than space between groups.
A short, fixed list of text sizes, each paired with a line height and weight and given a named job such as Title, Body or Caption, used consistently across every screen.
A measure of the luminance difference between two colors, from 1:1 to 21:1. WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text and essential non-text elements.
A Figma container with its own size, fill, clipping, constraints and optional auto layout or layout guides. Screens, rows, buttons and cards are all built from frames.
A bundle of layers whose size is derived from its children. It has no fill, padding or auto layout of its own, so it suits loose visual clusters rather than interface parts.
Rules on a child of a regular frame that decide how it moves or stretches when the frame is resized, such as Left and right, Bottom, Center or Scale.
A frame setting that arranges children automatically in a vertical, horizontal or grid flow, with a set gap between them and padding around them, re-flowing whenever content changes.
In auto layout, gap is the space between sibling children, and padding is the space between the children and the edges of their parent frame. Both belong to the parent.
Auto layout sizing options. Hug contents sizes a frame to its children, Fill container takes the parent's available space, and Fixed keeps an exact size regardless of content.
An auto layout option for horizontal and vertical flows that moves children onto a new line when they no longer fit, useful for chips and tags on narrow screens.
A setting, formerly called absolute position, that takes one child out of its auto layout flow so it can be positioned with constraints, such as a badge on an icon's corner.
A visual aid attached to a frame, formerly called a layout grid, in the form of columns, rows or a uniform grid, defined by count, margin and gutter. It never moves layers by itself.
A spacing convention where sizes and spacing are multiples of 8, with 4 as a half step, so values scale cleanly across screen densities and teams choose from a short list.
A width at which a layout changes its structure, such as a stats grid going from two to four columns. Good breakpoints come from where the content stops working, not from device lists.
The source definition of a reusable Figma element. Changes to it flow to every linked instance, except for properties an instance has overridden.
A linked copy of a main component. It can override content and appearance such as text, fills, visibility and nested instances, but cannot change its layer structure.
One version of a component inside a component set, described by variant properties such as State=Done, used for differences that restyle several layers together.
A switch on a component that instances can change without new variants: boolean for visibility, text for editable strings, instance swap for nested components, and slots for flexible content areas.
A named single value in Figma, such as a color, number, string or boolean, that can be bound to layer properties, alias another variable and hold different values per mode.
A variable named by its role, such as color/action/primary, that aliases a raw palette value. Components bind to semantic tokens so themes and palette changes stay one edit.
A named, reusable composite of visual properties in Figma, such as a text style's font, size, weight and line height, or an effect style holding stacked shadows.
One column of values in a variable collection, such as Light or Dark. Setting a mode on a frame or page swaps every bound value at once, and children inherit it.
A published Figma file whose components, styles and variables other files can use. Subscribing files are told about updates and choose when to accept them.
A component set with prototype interactions between its variants, such as On tap Change to Done, so every instance responds in prototypes without extra screens.
A prototype animation that matches layers with the same name and hierarchy in two frames and animates the differences in position, size, rotation, opacity and fill.
The tappable area of an interactive element. WCAG 2.2 AA requires at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels; Apple recommends 44 points and Material 48 dp.
A Dev Mode status on sections, frames or components that signals a design is stable enough to build. Edits afterwards automatically mark it as Changed.
A structured session where people evaluate a design against its stated goals, offering observations, effects and questions rather than personal preferences or approval.
